newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland, EU discuss differences over trade, cars.
newsitem.headline: Poland, EU discuss differences over trade, cars.

text.p: Officials of the European Union and the Polish government met in Warsaw on Thursday to iron out differences over trade policies and rules of car assembly by foreign companies in Poland.

Discussion at the meeting was expected to focus on EU's objections to a deal by which Poland has allowed South Korea's Daewoo group to import tens of thousands of car kits duty-free a year for assembly as part of its purchase last year of the FSO car plant in Warsaw.
"Today we will have more disccusion on this subject," Danuta Hubner, the secretary of the government's European Integration Committee, told reporters before the meeting.
EU manufacturers say the Daewoo deal gives a major Asian rival back-door entry into Europe and breaches the spirit of Poland's association agreement with the union.
She earlier said other issues to be discussed included trade difficulties and EU financial help to Poland in adjusting its economy, notably its outdated farm sector, to the community's standards.
The results of the meeting of the so-called Association Committee will be presented at a news conference on Friday, the government press office said.
Poland aims to begin talks on joining the European Union early next year, once the bloc's 15 members finish their inter-governmental conference.
